Title: Banana fritter trader arrested for threatening man with knife in Cheras
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 38-year-old man was arrested for threatening a trader with a knife during a disagreement over roadside business activities in Bandar Tasik Selatan, Cheras, this afternoon.
Cheras police chief assistant commissioner Rosdi Daud said the incident occurred in front of Residensi Sateri, Jalan Tasik Selatan 21, a round 3pm, when a man was allegedly slapped and threatened with a knife.
He said the suspect was detained at a nearby banana fritter stall to assist in the investigation, and police also seized the knife believed to have been used in the incident.
"Preliminary checks revealed that the suspect has no prior criminal record, and the case is being investigated under Section 323 and Section 506 of the Penal Code," he said in a statement.
He added that the investigation paper is currently being finalised, which includes recording statements from the victim and witnesses, as well as securing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage around the scene of the incident.
Earlier, a video depicting the incident went viral on social media.

Title: Hackers steal US$112mil from French bank
Article:
PARIS: French lender Credit Mutuel Arkea said on Thursday hackers had stolen around €100 million (US$112.61 million) in a cyber heist and it was working to try to recover the money, in a rare case of cybercriminals successfully stealing from a mainstream bank.
The cyberattack, which was made public on Wednesday, follows the theft last week of US$6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance and a wave of cyberattacks targeting internet-connected fridges in Europe. French prosecutors said they were investigating the heist.
The attackers used an account belonging to Credit Mutuel Arkea to carry out "fraudulent transactions", Credit Mutuel Arkea said in a statement on Wednesday. The funds were not in the form of cryptocurrency, the bank said, but could have been converted to crypto after being stolen.
Credit Mutuel Arkea temporarily suspended some transactions as a precaution, resulting in delays to some transfers, but said customer assets were not affected.
A spokesperson rejected media reports that its online banking subsidiary Fortuneo was the entry point for the attack, saying that neither the division nor its customers' accounts were involved.
Cyber experts told Reuters that while cyberattacks are common, it was unusual for money to be stolen virtually from a bank.
Rafay Baloch, CEO of cybersecurity and security engineering firm RedSecLabs, said the Credit Mutuel attack was unprecedented in Europe.
"We're seeing a lot of these sophisticated attacks targeted at the application layer and sophisticated social engineering attacks being targeted at banking institutions," he said.
FRANCE OPENS INVESTIGATION
The Paris prosecutor's office said its cybercrime unit received a complaint from Credit Mutuel Arkea on Wednesday and immediately opened an investigation, led by France's cybercrime police.
Credit Mutuel Arkea's spokesperson declined to identify the third-party service provider whose platform was used in the attack and said it had informed the European Central Bank, French banking supervisors and prosecutors. France's banking regulator, the ACPR, declined to comment.
While successful hacks of large financial institutions are rare, financial regulators globally have stepped up warnings about the risk of cyberattacks, particularly with the growth of AI.
"Any time you have a hit in the financial system, it's a big deal," said Puneet Kakkar, Managing Director at Nardello & Co in Paris.
Brittany-based Credit Mutuel Arkea is a French co-operative banking group with more than 5.8 million customers and €211.5 billion in assets. It is part of the wider Credit Mutuel banking network and is affiliated with its central body, while retaining significant strategic autonomy.
French banks typically have strong cybersecurity, due to regulatory requirements, said Kakkar. Still, he said, "cybercriminals are becoming more opportunistic and more creative."
In 2016, attackers stole US$81 million from the Bangladesh central bank account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Millions of dollars' worth of funds have also previously been stolen from banks in Russia and India during cyberattacks, Reuters has reported.--REUTERS

Title: Johari: Lynas-US cooperation to facilitate rare earth supply agreement
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Cooperation between Lynas Rare Earths Ltd (Australia) and the United States government aims to facilitate a material supply agreement for the advanced manufacturing industry.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said this would support US efforts to achieve its national supply chain resilience objectives.
He said Lynas Malaysia had informed him that the agreement was a commercial arrangement handled directly by its subsidiary, Lynas LLC USA, with the US.
He said the supply of the rare earth oxides was intended for research and development (R&D) in the permanent magnet manufacturing sector, which the US is currently exploring.
"Within the complex value chain of the rare earth elements (REE) industry, Lynas Malaysia's operations are at the initial processing stage, involving the separation of raw REE mined in Australia into rare earth oxide (REO) supplies.
"After processing, the REO is supplied to metal manufacturers overseas, who then channel it to magnet producers. The magnets produced are subsequently used as inputs by electric motor manufacturers and original equipment manufacturers (OEMs)," he said in a written reply published on the Parliament website.
He was responding to a question from Shaharizukirnain Abd Kadir (PN-Setiu) regarding the government's stance on the US$96 million (RM388 million) REO supply agreement between Lynas and the Pentagon.
Johari said Lynas Malaysia's processing operations comply with the government's current policies, including operational and manufacturing licence requirements, as well as Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) approval.
"This also includes a commitment to developing the midstream and downstream segments of the ecosystem, with priority given to the development of local companies," he said.
He said his ministry is committed to developing the midstream and downstream segments of the REE industry to establish a holistic and integrated ecosystem, while maximising the economic value of the country's mineral resources.
"The strategy focuses on attracting domestic and international investments to develop and subsequently strengthen the midstream and downstream segments of the REE industry.
"This is particularly in high-technology manufacturing, such as permanent magnets, advanced materials, electronic components and batteries," he said.
Johari said potential REE investors are currently reluctant to invest due to the lack of guarantees of a stable domestic supply of REE raw materials.
He said the government had agreed to allow flexibility in the existing moratorium policy on the export of raw REE materials through the Guidelines for Consideration of Applications to Export Raw Rare Earth Elements.
"This flexibility in exports is limited solely to R&D activities. Companies must demonstrate a clear commitment to collaborating on the development of processing facilities in Malaysia within three years from the date of approval to export raw REE materials," he said.
Johari said Malaysia needed to leverage strategic partnerships and technology transfers, both domestically and internationally, including from partner countries with experience in REE processing, to realise its ambition of developing the industry.
"This move will strengthen local capabilities across the entire value chain, from mining activities to the manufacturing of finished products.
"Furthermore, it will position Malaysia as a key player in the global critical minerals supply chain," he said.

Title: Anis Rizana, Armed Forces chief among 218 Perak honours recipients
Article:
IPOH: Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry secretary-general Datuk Anis Rizana Mohd Zainudin heads the list of 218 recipients of state honours and medals on the occasion of the 70th birthday of Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah today.
Anis Rizana, a former director-general of the Customs Department, will receive the Darjah Seri Paduka Mahkota Perak, which carries the title Datuk Seri.
Armed Forces chief General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman will receive the Darjah Datuk Seri Panglima Taming Sari, also carrying the title Datuk Seri, while Accountant-General Nasran Omar will receive the Darjah Datuk Paduka Cura Si Manja Kini, which carries the title Datuk.
The Darjah Datuk Paduka Mahkota Perak, which  carries the title Datuk, will be conferred on 14 recipients, including state executive council member Sandrea Ng Shy Ching, Ipoh Mayor Zamakhshari Hanipah and Bernama editor-in-chief D.R. Arul Rajoo.
Eight recipients, including Perak deputy police chief Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Azlin Sadari, will receive the Darjah Datuk Pahlawan Taming Sari, which carries the title Datuk Pahlawan.
The other awards comprise the Darjah Ahli Paduka Cura Si Manja Kini  for 10 recipients, Darjah Ahli Paduka Mahkota Perak  for 28, Darjah Ahli Cura Si Manja Kini (ACM) for 18, and Darjah Ahli Mahkota Perak  for 47.
Bernama's Perak bureau chief Syamsiah Shat will be among the ACM recipients.
[[nid:1571799]]
The state will also confer the Pingat Pekerti Terpilih  on 49 recipients, Pingat Jasa Kebaktian  on 31 and Pingat Lama Perkhidmatan  on 10.
Orang Kaya Bendahara Seri Maharaja Tan Sri Dr Mohd Zahidi Zainuddin said the investiture ceremonies would be held in two sessions.
The first, involving awards carrying titles, is scheduled for Nov 15, while the second, for awards without titles, will take place on Nov 21. Both ceremonies will be held at Balairung Seri, Istana Iskandariah, Kuala Kangsar.
He urged the people to mark the sultan's birthday by flying the state flag at office buildings, business premises and homes, as well as putting up lights as a sign of loyalty to the ruler.
Zahidi also said Sultan Nazrin had sponsored a special lunch today for inmates and detainees serving sentences in Perak.
The initiative involves 8,960 inmates and detainees at Tapah Prison, Taiping Prison, Kamunting Correctional Centre, Batu Gajah Correctional and Rehabilitation Centre, Chenderiang Correctional Centre, Kuala Kangsar Satellite Prison and Perak Halfway House.
The programme would be coordinated by the Perak Prisons Department, he added.

Title: France workers strike, march for 'dignified wage'
Article:
PARIS: Thousands of striking workers protested across France on Thursday against the rising cost of living in a new escalation following weeks of demonstrations, with police firing tear gas as violence and vandalism broke out in some cities.
More than 270,000 people had already taken to the streets across the country, the interior ministry reported, before a major march kicked off in Paris from 2pm (1300 GMT).
The demonstrations come as the eurozone's second largest economy battles to redress its finances, six months ahead of elections to replace centrist President Emmanuel Macron, with the far right leading in opinion polls.
The high school student movement that began with youths protesting over learning conditions has coincided with widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, which culminated on Oct 17 in the worst rioting France has seen in years.
"The question today is not whether we're going to win" but rather "how much we're going to win", CGT union leader Sophie Binet said at the Paris rally.
The unions are calling for across-the-board wage raises, tax reforms and better learning conditions for young people and have complained about police restrictions on certain protests.
While the marches were largely peaceful, skirmishes between protestors and police broke out in some cities, including Lyon where at least one vehicle was torched and tear gas was fired.
Winegrower Martin Thiberge said he wanted to take part in demonstrations that were drawing together people from across French society.
"We want to make a living from our work, to make a dignified wage," he said at the Lyon protest.
In Marseille, 31-year-old social worker Lea told AFP that she was "fed up with counting every cent."
"This social movement has given us hope," she added.
In Paris, the Eiffel Tower and the Arc de Triomphe, popular among tourists, were closed for the day.
- SCHOOL BLOCKADES -
Dozens of high-schoolers protested in several cities, with the government reporting blockades at 81 out of the country's 3,700 high schools.
A high school student association said classes had been suspended at 1,000 secondary schools.
Around 16 per cent of teachers nationwide were on strike, the education ministry said.
In Paris, police used tear gas to try to prevent students from blocking access to the Helene-Boucher high school in the city's east, an AFP reporter said.
Public and private education unions have called for strike action, as well as unions representing rail workers, public hospitals and postal services.
At the capital's Montparnasse train station, a psychologist who gave her name as Jeanne said her trip had been delayed.
"It's tedious to get up early, wait, and then see your train cancelled, but it's understandable there's a strike," she said.
- POLICE VIOLENCE ALLEGED -
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez announced Wednesday that 70,000 police officers and security forces would be deployed across the country, promising "an extremely firm response" to any "acts of violence" or disorder.
The protests have been largely peaceful, though some disintegrated into clashes with police, who have fired tear gas and water cannon.
An attempted murder investigation has been launched after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces in Paris on Saturday.
The police response has been criticised as heavy-handed and internal police investigations have been launched over allegations of brutality.
Several teenage protesters have been seriously wounded and thousands arrested.
Similar protests have erupted in other European countries in recent weeks.--AFP

Title: KKDW reallocates RM200mil from rural housing to settle road project arrears
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Constraints in implementing the Sejahtera People's Housing Programme (PPRS) have prompted the Rural and Regional Development Ministry to reallocate RM200 million from its 2026 allocation to settle outstanding payments for rural road projects.
Deputy Minister Datuk Rubiah Wang said the constraints included land ownership disputes among heirs, a lack of suitable sites and overlapping applicants' names.
She said the reallocation was carried out through a Notice of Change (NOC) from the original PPRS 2026 allocation of RM413 million to prevent the annual allocation from going unspent due to project delays.
However, Rubiah said the adjustment did not mean the ministry was sidelining its welfare agenda and the provision of housing for rural communities.
"Applications for PPRS are indeed very high, but we face various implementation issues on the ground... that is why some projects have had to be postponed and we need to re-examine them, which is why the RM200 million could not be spent.
"That means we can issue a NOC for rural road projects. That is why I said earlier that we are not sacrificing the interests of any particular project," she said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 and the Development Expenditure Estimates 2027 at the committee stage for the ministry in the Dewan Rakyat.
For the 2027 Budget, she said the government allocated RM416.2 million for PPRS, which is expected to benefit 12,457 recipients through new housing and home repair projects nationwide.
On rural road projects, Rubiah said implementation had also been affected by a Finance Ministry directive on Sept 10 last year to defer the issuance of Letters of Acceptance (LOA) as a spending control measure.
She said the deferment was for the ministry to stabilise its financial position and settle commitments on earlier projects, but the absence of a fixed timeline from MoF risked causing new project tenders to be cancelled.
"An LOA is valid for only two to three months. If we do not obtain further approval from MoF within six months, the project tender will certainly have to be cancelled and we will need to start a new process," she said.
Under the guidelines for the preparation of the 13th Malaysia Plan, projects that are not tendered or implemented within two years risk being cancelled, she added.
Citing Sabah as an example, she said the issuance of SSTs for 20 rural road projects at the pre-implementation stage were frozen, while 62 projects in the construction phase would proceed.
The Dewan Rakyat then approved the 2027 operating and development expenditure estimates for the ministry, amounting to RM4,850,160,200 under Budget 2027, by a majority vote after 31 MPs debated the estimates.
Before adjourning the sitting, Dewan Rakyat Deputy Speaker Datuk Seri Dr Ramli Mohd Nor took the opportunity to wish all members of the House and Malaysians a Happy Deepavali.
He also announced that the Dewan Rakyat would not sit next Monday and Tuesday, with proceedings resuming on Wednesday.

Title: No notice yet on special or regular Negri Sembilan assembly sitting — assemblyman
Article:
JELEBU: No notice has been issued for either a special or regular sitting of the Negri Sembilan sstate legislative assembly, says Klawang assemblyman Danni Rais.
He said the assembly secretary had yet to notify members of any scheduled sitting.
"However, I believe it is important for the state assembly to convene to table the state budget, as it is closely linked to the people's interests," he said when met at a Deepavali aid event in Kuala Klawang.
Danni said the state budget would determine the state's future, and all parties should make the right decisions in the best interests of Negri Sembilan residents.
He said the priority now should be to address the people's needs.
Asked whether the Budget might not be tabled due to certain circumstances, Danni said he did not wish to interfere in the affairs of others, including the menteri besar, as an ordinary assemblyman.
"Everyone, including the people of the state, hopes the state budget can be tabled.
"I also understand that the menteri besar is doing his best. We are not trying to pressure anyone, given how complicated the current situation is.
"I believe the menteri besar is taking and will continue to take the best steps for the state's future," he said.
On the contents of theBudget, Danni said assemblymen from Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional had previously held a meeting to discuss the state budget.
"Personally, I believe the draft budget is the best for the people of the state, should it be tabled," he said.

Title: Three more tankers damaged in Hormuz as Iran steps up pressure on Trump
Article:
DUBAI: Iran reported three more tankers had been damaged in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, making clear that shipping would remain in peril as long as the war in the Gulf is unresolved, now that US voters have punished President Donald Trump for waging it.
The electoral rout that cost Trump's Republicans control of Congress has prompted a stark reassessment of the conflict's political cost in Washington, led by Vice President JD Vance, who said in a long social media post on Wednesday that the war was to blame for his party's defeat.
In a mocking reply on Thursday, Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, Vance's opposite number at previous peace talks, accused Vance of letting Trump double down like a "losing gambler" by planning more US strikes.
If Vance believed the war was a mistake he should persuade Trump to call it off, Qalibaf said: "Skip the TED talk. Why not say this to your boss?"
Oil prices have plunged in recent days as traders wagered that Trump, chastened by voters, may be less likely to restart the strikes he launched alongside Israel as "Operation Epic Fury" in February. Prices bounced back slightly on Thursday but are down more than US$20 a barrel from last week.
Iranian officials have been meeting with Qatari mediators since last week to discuss proposals to end the hostilities. But neither side has announced any breakthroughs on the major issues that have prevented any peace agreement so far.
ATTACKS ON TANKERS AT RECORD PACE
Meanwhile, attacks on tankers in the Gulf are still running close to a record pace. At least five vessels have reported incidents since Sunday, according to UK maritime security agency UKMTO, around the same rate as in October when the agency said 35 vessels were hit, the most of any month of the war.
The UKMTO reported that a vessel had been struck by two unidentified projectiles late on Wednesday.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards, who do not typically acknowledge firing on merchant ships but say the transit route is unsafe without Teheran's consent, said two tankers had struck naval mines and another had caught fire on Thursday.
On Wednesday Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei said there should not be "even the slightest inclination towards submission" to the United States, which he said would remain hostile towards Iran no matter which party was in power.
'HE IS PLANNING TO BOMB IRAN'
When asked about Vance's comments on the war on Wednesday, Trump defended the decision to launch it, saying it was important to prevent Iran from getting a nuclear weapon, a justification he has repeatedly cited.
A White House adviser told Reuters that some officials and staff inside the White House viewed Vance's post as a foreign policy break from the president and a public recognition of the war's economic consequences.
But two sources told Reuters they believed Trump was still likely to order resumed hostilities.
"He is planning to bomb Iran. Don't listen to what he's saying. He held off because of the midterms. We asked him to hold off until the midterms," said one of the sources. The other said Trump did not ​have anything to lose politically now ⁠that the midterms were over.
Peacemaking efforts have revolved around the future status of the strait, a US blockade on Iranian ports, sanctions on the Islamic Republic and a resumption of negotiations over Teheran's nuclear programme.
A senior Iranian official said this week that the two sides remain far apart.
Qatar said on Tuesday that the United States and Iran were committed to mediation efforts and were reviewing proposals aimed at bridging their differences, adding that there had been developments in talks with both sides.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Shah Alam at risk of major floods without alternative waterways, says Khir Toyo
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Shah Alam remains at risk of major flooding unless alternative waterways are built to divert excess rainwater from existing rivers, says former Selangor menteri besar Dr Mohamad Khir Toyo
He said the risk was likely to increase due to rapid development in surrounding areas and Shah Alam's lower elevation compared with neighbouring areas.
He said a detailed study of the proposed Canal City flood mitigation project, which he planned during his tenure, found that it could hold hundreds of thousands of litres of water and protect Shah Alam from major floods for up to 100 years.
The project involved building an 18km canal linking Sungai Klang and Sungai Langat.
[[nid:1571788]]
The canal was also designed to incorporate two former mining lakes, one each in Shah Alam and Kuala Langat, as water retention areas before the accumulated water was channelled to the sea when the tide receded.
"In addition, residential areas were planned along the canal, with homes surrounded by rivers or smaller canals.
"Unfortunately, the project was cancelled and, worse still, the land was sold to developers," he said in a statement today.
Khir Toyo said Shah Alam was situated in a low-lying valley compared with surrounding areas such as Sungai Buloh, Rawang and Petaling Jaya.
"Major floods are likely when heavy rain coincides with high tides.
"When sea levels are higher than river levels, rainwater filling the rivers cannot flow out to sea.
"This causes water to accumulate and stagnate in low-lying areas such as Shah Alam," he said.
He said rapid development in Kuala Selangor, Sungai Buloh, Rawang and Petaling Jaya had also increased water runoff into low-lying areas of Shah Alam, particularly Kampung Melayu Subang, Batu Tiga and Sri Muda.
"As long as the government does not provide outlets for rainwater, such as retention ponds or storage rivers capable of holding hundreds of millions of litres of water while waiting for the tide to recede, Shah Alam remains at risk of major flooding even when there is no heavy rain in the area," he said.

Title: Melaka election: Choose candidates who have 'direct line' to PM's Office, says Anwar
Article:
MELAKA: Voters in the Melaka election should choose elected representatives who have a "direct line" to the Prime Minister's Office to ensure smooth development processes and the protection of residents' welfare.
Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said good relations and alignment of direction between the federal administration and assemblymen were vital to ensuring the smooth implementation of development projects and public welfare policies.
Citing the PH candidates for the Paya Rumput and Kelebang seats as examples, Anwar said both candidates share the same direction as the federal government, and their credibility and integrity are greatly needed to effectively translate government policies at the grassroots level.
"I look after the country, and I want those who represent us to help follow this line — they must follow this policy. So can our representative here, Tok Man (Datuk Azman Abidin) in Paya Rumput help?
"Let there be a direct voice to my office. Similarly with our young female candidate (Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir) in Kelebang — pleasing in appearance, good at work, and hardworking," he said.
Anwar said this when delivering his speech at the Ceramah Perdana Melaka Rumah Kita for the Paya Rumput seat here tonight.
He said, having elected representatives who possess a "direct line" and close working relationship with the nation's top leadership provides a major advantage to voters in bringing any infrastructure, drainage, or socioeconomic issues directly to the government's attention.
Therefore, Anwar reminded voters in Melaka to make wise assessments when choosing leadership by electing candidates who truly work for the people, rather than those who merely stoke sentiments throughout the campaign.
Meanwhile, speaking at a separate event while attending the Madani Sinar Deepavali Celebration at the Kampung Permai Main Hall in Machap Umboo here, he said he was optimistic that PH can secure a victory in the Nov 14 election.
"I know they say, 'Oh, Melaka is not a PH stronghold.' I know it's not a PH stronghold... Selangor was never a PH stronghold before either, nor was Perak.
"Yes, (politics) has ebbs and flows, but this time I believe we can start bringing change — we start bringing change here in Melaka to save the country," he said.

Title: Bomb hoaxes hit 27 flights across Europe, trigger fighter jet escorts
Article:
ROME: Hoax bomb threats hit at least 27 affected flights around Europe on Thursday from Ireland to Bulgaria, the second wave this week, forcing some to make unplanned landings and prompting fighter jets to escort or intercept others.
While no country has attributed blame for the threats, ⁠they come as many European officials are accusing Russia of masterminding sabotage and "hybrid attacks" — often cheap, easily deniable and not expected to trigger an armed response.
Denmark, Poland and Romania, all affected by Thursday's disruptions, have previously accused Moscow directly, while Germany blamed Russia for an attack on Leipzig airport in August. Britain has blamed Russia in the past but linked Iran to a suspected plot to attack a US air base. Both Russia and Iran deny any involvement.
Eric Schouten, head of the aviation security group Dyami, said most of the countries affected supported Ukraine in its war against Russia's invasion.
"From a geopolitical view, I'm thinking, you always have to think about the scenario of hybrid warfare, where a country in this way — today we are looking at Russia, right? — is attacking us on multiple fronts, from railways to supermarkets to blood banks, most recently. The energy sector, the internet sector, and the aviation sector are among those," he said.
FLIGHTS TO MILAN, ROME, PARIS, PRAGUE, SOFIA AFFECTED
Over France, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu's office said he had sent fighter jets to intercept an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome and escort it to an air force base at Evreux after the pilot did not cooperate with authorities as expected. No reason was given for the pilot's behaviour.
Bulgaria's air force said its fighter jets had escorted three airliners to the ground. Ryanair planes from Copenhagen and Madrid to Sofia landed as planned while a flight from London to Sofia was diverted to Plovdiv, Bulgaria's second city.
Spanish authorities received three emailed bomb threats in under 20 minutes involving two Air Europa departures from Madrid to Paris and four inbound Iberia flights from Rome and Milan, Spain's Guardia Civil said.
Several aircraft in Madrid were halted or returned to their stands and passengers were disembarked while planes were inspected.
In Warsaw, a LOT flight to Paris was stopped as it taxied towards take-off and passengers were transferred to another aircraft. A flight from Cork in Ireland was delayed 90 minutes after the airport received a threat, the airport operator said.
At Copenhagen airport in Denmark, two planes were searched, police said.
Italian media reported that a Wizz Air flight from Milan to Warsaw had been diverted to Vienna.
Two Easyjet flights from Britain, one flight from Ireland and one from Greece landed as scheduled in Prague after receiving bomb threats, as did a Finnair flight from Helsinki to Vienna, a Polish LOT flight from Warsaw to Brussels, a Hungarian Wizz Air  flight from Milan to Bucharest, and an Air Serbia flight from Belgrade, also to Bucharest.
The Italian news agency ANSA said two planes had landed as planned in Milan, while a person familiar with the matter said Italy's air force escorted a Finnair plane coming from Helsinki to its scheduled landing in Rome.
The operator of Rome's Fiumicino Airport said there had been no disruption to services, and that departing passengers were philosophical.
"It's more complicated with everything that's going on, but what else are we going to do?" said Spaniard Lucia Parga. "We still have to get around. So, well, we just have to deal with it as best we can."
Another traveller, Gabriele Franzese, added: "You can't worry too much about every piece of news. If the plane crashes, so be it. If it's meant to happen, it'll happen anyway."
CYBERATTACKS ON SUPERMARKETS AND BLOOD BANKS
Joji Waites, director of flight safety for the British Airline Pilots' Association, said it was industry practice that airlines did not act on threats unless they had been rated credible by assessors.
Eliran Almog, CEO of aviation cybersecurity firm Cyviation, said the hoaxes could serve both to disrupt operations and to observe how airlines, airports and authorities respond.
"These aviation threats are also occurring in the same period as cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems across Europe," Almog said.
"Different essential services are experiencing disruption that carries economic costs and can undermine public confidence."
On Tuesday, at least seven flights and a cruise ship received hoaxthreats.
This week, unidentified hackers for the second time shut down fridges in supermarkets in several European countries, also affecting French blood banks.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Traffic smooth on major highways as of 10pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Traffic on major highways heading out of the Klang Valley was generally smooth and under control as of 10pm tonight.
A Malaysian Highway Authority spokesman said there were minor congestion reported at several locations following accidents and an increase in vehicle volume.
"For northbound traffic along the North-South Expressway, congestion was reported over a 4km stretch between Sungkai and Slim River, as well as along a one-kilometre stretch at the Menora Tunnel heading towards Kuala Kangsar, due to accidents.
"Congestion was also reported at Juru heading towards Perai and on the Penang Bridge heading towards Perai," the spokesman told Bernama when contacted.
For southbound traffic, congestion was detected at Sedenak heading towards Kulai, while traffic along the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway and East Coast Expressway 1 (LPT1) remained smooth.
The spokesman said MHA expected traffic congestion to build up tomorrow night following the announcement of a 50 per cent toll discount from Nov 6 to 7 in conjunction with Deepavali this Sunday.

Title: Trump's Iran war gamble backfires as voters weaken his grip on power
Article:
Trump went to war seeking regime change in Iran. Instead, it was his own grip on Washington that gave way, as voters weary of the war and hit by soaring fuel prices handed Democrats control of Congress.
That leaves a weakened president facing a choice between a negotiated exit and a riskier escalation.
In Teheran and among its allies, the result was swiftly cast as a verdict on the conflict. Across the Gulf, officials were left wondering which way Trump would turn.
"Iran succeeded in regime change in America" was the first reaction of one source close to a US Gulf ally.
Officials in the Gulf states were stunned into silence by the scale of the Democratic sweep in Tuesday's US midterm elections, said the source.
The war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Feb 28 spread across the region as Teheran fired missiles and drones at Gulf targets and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting global energy supplies.
The US-Israeli campaign damaged Iran's military capabilities but failed to deliver a decisive outcome, leaving the issue of Iran's nuclear programme unresolved.
A weakened Trump, facing a Democratic Congress able to constrain his military options, has greater incentive to seek a deal, said two sources close to Gulf government circles.
A full-scale assault on Iran now looks less likely, they said.
Further limited strikes on nuclear facilities may offer the US a way to claim its objectives had been met and draw a line under the conflict, as China steps up efforts to broker a settlement.
Yet an agreement that allows Iran to claim clear victory and leaves Trump looking defeated can provoke recklessness as readily as restraint, said Gulf analysts.
The rebuke from the US electorate came a week after voters delivered their own blow to the war's other architect, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
His right-wing bloc won 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats in the Oct 27 election, eight short of a majority, leaving him fighting to retain power.
"The US election results make a settlement more urgent for Trump, but no easier for Iran," said Ebtesam al-Ketbi, president of the Emirates Policy Center in Abu Dhabi.
Gulf states want the election to open a path to ending the war, but not at any cost, said al-Ketbi.
In Teheran, leaders savoured Trump's humiliation but did not lower their guard, with Iran's chief negotiator hailing a "NO TO WAR" result.
Two senior sources said Teheran remained on high alert, fearing Trump could try to make up for his defeat with a military strike.
Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned against "even the slightest inclination towards submission", a signal that Iran has no intention of softening its demands over the Strait of Hormuz.
Abdulaziz Sager, chairman of the Saudi-based Gulf Research Center, warned that defeat could make Trump more willing to strike, not less.
With the midterms behind him and no third term ahead, the electoral considerations that once encouraged restraint have diminished.
That leaves a president with less to lose and a legacy to secure.
Trump, he said, may see confrontation with Iran as a chance to "finish the job" before leaving office.
"If Iran continues to resist... and emerges claiming victory, Trump may feel compelled to act to prevent that outcome and claim a clear success for his presidency."
Lebanese political commentator Sarkis Naoum said Trump's defeat had weakened his hand with Iran, leaving him with diminished leverage at the negotiating table and fewer options to secure a deal.
An official from Iran-backed Hizbollah said the threat of war had not necessarily receded and that "reckless moves" remained a possibility.
"At this moment, the chances of escalation and de-escalation may be equal," he said.
Once seated in Congress in January, Democrats are expected to use their power to investigate Trump's administration, family and allies and demand concessions on major legislation.
For US allies in the Gulf, the political shift in Washington carries risks that extend well beyond the war itself.
A source close to government thinking said Gulf states were wary of probes that they expected to be launched into business by their own entities with the Trump family.
The writer is from Reuters

Title: US election puts decades of bipartisan support for Israel under strain
Article:
Democrats' take over of Congress and growing Republican unease over Israel could trigger the biggest reassessment of United States support for its closest Middle East ally in decades, after an election shaped in part by anger over the Iran war.
Democrats won both the Senate and House in Tuesday's midterms. Many winning candidates were progressives who campaigned against military aid to Israel and the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Israel's campaign in Gaza and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's embrace of President Donald Trump and other Republicans had already strained decades of bipartisan support for Israel.
Democratic control could bring greater scrutiny of military aid and West Bank violence, along with hearings and challenges to Trump nominees, although the president's veto limits the party's ability to force major policy changes.
One successful progressive was Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, the first Muslim elected to the US Senate despite Republican attempts to win over Jewish voters who might have been uncomfortable with his faith and his criticism of Israel.
There were also signs that Republicans might reexamine their party's traditional support for Israel.
Vice-President JD Vance on Wednesday blamed the election rout on the war against Iran and identified Israel as an issue for Republicans.
He said in a social media post that one pollster identified four actions that would bring disgruntled Trump voters back: "1) End the war 2) Focus on cost of living/inflation 3) Put America First 4) Change our relationship to Israel."
Trump announced in a Fox News interview on Tuesday that he had made a deal with Netanyahu that Washington would end annual security assistance to Israel.
Policy towards Israel has emerged as a generational divide in US politics.
Opinion polls show younger voters, including some Republicans, feel the country has been too supportive of Israel and insufficiently supportive of residents of the Palestinian territories.
Congressional sentiment had already been shifting.
In September, 46 of the 47 members of the Senate Democratic caucus voted for a resolution to force Trump's administration to report to Congress on increasing violence against Palestinians by Israeli settlers in the West Bank.
Republicans blocked the measure, but the near-unanimous Democratic vote was a sharp departure from decades of reliable bipartisan backing for Israel.
Democrats will likely focus again on West Bank violence.
"We need to make sure that we apply our laws and international law and our policies uniformly across the board when it comes to the actions of countries.
"There should not be an Israel exception," said Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, who has led attempts to put human rights conditions on Israel aid.
Democrats' power remains limited, however. Trump promised to be "Mr. Veto", and they are unlikely to muster the two-thirds majorities needed to override his vetoes if the president refuses to sign their bills.
Still, there might be enough resistance to sending US tax dollars abroad, and anger over the Iran war, for the "America First" wing of the Republican Party to also push back.
The election result could see "weird bedfellows of left and right come together in condemnation of Israel", said Price Floyd, a former US official and senior adviser with Argyll Strategy, a London-based strategic communications firm.
Majorities also mean Democrats can summon administration officials to public hearings, a rarity under Trump's Republicans.
Opinion polls showed the Iran war was a top election issue. Many Americans blamed higher prices — especially for petrol — on the conflict Trump began in February.
Jonathan Schanzer, executive director of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies think tank, which advocates for a strong US-Israel alliance, said Israel's changing leadership could change the "mood music" of dealings between the two countries.
Netanyahu lost his governing majority in an Oct 27 Israeli election, but denied opponents a clear path to unseat him. Negotiations to form a new government are expected to be protracted.
A new Israeli government, particularly one less closely tied to Republicans, could engage in a more cooperative way with Democrats.
"Nothing is going to change in the US until January when Congress takes their seats and by then, there may be a new Israeli government that would also have an impact on this," said Schanzer.
The writer is from Reuters

Title: Five-day high tide phenomenon expected in Klang from Saturday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Klang residents have been asked to remain vigilant as a five-day high tide phenomenon is expected to begin this Saturday, with sea levels at Port Klang forecast to reach 5.2 metres.
The Klang Disaster Management Committee said the phenomenon was expected to last from Nov 7 to 11, with the highest tide forecast at 5.02am on Sunday, reaching the warning level.
Under the Port Klang water-level indicators, readings of between 5.0 and 5.3 metres are classified as warning level, while readings of 5.4 to 5.5 metres are considered dangerous
The sea level is forecast to reach 5.1 metres at 4.23am on Saturday before rising to 5.2 metres at 5.02am on Sunday.
It is then expected to reach 5.1 metres at 5.37am on Monday and 6.08am on Tuesday, before dropping to 5.0 metres at 6.37am on Wednesday.
Afternoon high tides are forecast to range between 4.0 and 4.8 metres throughout the period, with peak readings expected between 4.53pm on Saturday and 7.02pm on Wednesday.
The weather forecast also indicates thunderstorms in several areas on Saturday and Sunday afternoons, followed by rain in some places at night.
From Monday to Wednesday, thunderstorms are expected in most areas in the afternoons, while rain is forecast in many areas at night.
The committee urged residents to make the necessary preparations and remain alert to their surroundings throughout the period.
The sea-level and weather forecasts are based on information from the Malaysian Meteorological Department and the National Hydrographic Centre.
Members of the public can call the emergency hotline at 999 or the Klang Disaster Operations Centre at 03-3382 9292 in the event of an emergency.

Title: Grab to cut driver fees, cap deductions at 32pct in Vietnam
Article:
HANOI: Vietnam's competition commission said on Thursday that ride-hailing firm Grab had agreed to cut some fees charged to passengers and drivers and compensate drivers affected by excessive deductions.
The announcement follows the government watchdog's preliminary review of complaints from drivers between late August and mid-September about declining fares, commissions and other deductions that they said were hurting earnings.
Grab proposed six measures, including a small reduction in app usage fees charged to drivers and capping the combined fees it collects at no more than 32 per cent of the total amount paid by passengers.
The company will also reimburse about 3.9 billion dong (US$151,869) to drivers after finding about 0.13 per cent of trips since 2024 had deductions above 35 per cent, partly due to algorithm errors or supply-demand fluctuations, the commission said.
The review came after Grab drivers in September urged colleagues via social ​media to boycott the app for two days over falling earnings and opaque pricing and commission policies.
Grab plans to spend about 912 billion dong  (US$35.51 million) on driver incentives and operating-cost support and 1.8 trillion dong on passenger promotions in the fourth quarter, the watchdog said.
The watchdog said it would continue monitoring implementation of the measures and could take action if violations were found.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Malaysia's digital ambitions must not outpace cyber defences
Article:
Malaysia faces the threat of cyberattacks, warned Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
It is inevitable, driven by Malaysia's 30-year advancement to become Southeast Asia's digital powerhouse.
The boom started in 1996. The first commercial satellite, Measat-1, introduced direct-to-home satellite television.
Soon after, the Multimedia Super Corridor attracted global companies by offering special financial, tax and economic perks. The boom's trifecta was complete: dial-up Internet opened a borderless cyberspace and global e-commerce.
By 2010, the National Information Technology Agenda bridged the digital divide, shifting government counter services online.
In the following decade, high-speed broadband rolled out—digitising enterprises, training Malaysians for digital platforms and opening up social media.
In this decade, the Malaysia Digital Economy Blueprint produced hyper growth, a high-income digital economy and accelerated 5G mobilisation.
Global data centres propelling artificial intelligence are sprouting, including two of the world's biggest in Kempas and Nusantara in Johor, contributing to the gross domestic product through 2038.
According to the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation, investments under the Malaysia Digital national strategic initiative surged 125 per cent in the second quarter of 2025 to RM29.47 billion from RM13.11 billion in the first quarter.
This could explain the cyberattacks and the price of becoming a digital powerhouse. Since 2016, Malaysia has faced ransomware attacks, breaches of public infrastructure and government networks, and political hacking.
In 2017, 46 million mobile phone subscribers' records were offered for sale. In 2019, 28 million airline customer data records were exposed. In 2022, a domestic airline was hit by a ransomware attack.
In 2023 and 2024, websites were defaced, personal data and intellectual property stolen, and networks breached. In 2024, a ransomware attack hit our mass transit operator, with stolen data published on the dark web.
Last year, the Kuala Lumpur International Airport was hit by a US$10 million ransomware demand while another attack targeted government and private sector organisations.
Protecting the infrastructure powering our ambition is an urgent priority. The first step is raising the National Cyber Threat Level alongside a suite of immediate security measures: 24-hour monitoring, system patching, multi-factor authentication and updated service contingency plans.
The sober reality is that cyberattacks carry consequences well beyond the digital realm. Cybersecurity cannot be left entirely to the government. It requires shared responsibility.
The private sector must also help protect digital infrastructure. Since Malaysia's digital ambitions cannot outpace cyber defence, the real test lies in whether Malaysia can maintain essential services through the next major cyberattack.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Parliamentary inquiry considered over Indonesian Vice-President Gibran's education credentials
Article:
JAKARTA: Several Indonesian political parties are considering a parliamentary inquiry into the validity of Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's diploma as a rift intensifies between President Prabowo Subianto and his predecessor Joko Widodo, Gibran's father.
The proposal emerged after the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled that Gibran's foreign senior high school credentials did not meet domestic legal requirements for vice-presidential candidates, and had been improperly accepted by election officials.
It also followed the arrest of Prabowo's former chief of staff, Listyo Sigit Prabowo, in a wiretapping scandal that the government said could amount to treason. Listyo, also a former national police chief, was known as a Widodo loyalist.
Seven of the eight parties in parliament have joined Prabowo's coalition, giving him a majority. Neither Jokowi nor Gibran has a party represented in parliament.
Three parties within Prabowo's camp and one outside the coalition said they were currently considering three legislative courses of action, officials said.
Under the Constitution, lawmakers can seek an explanation from the government, launch an inquiry or investigation, or formally express their position on alleged legal or constitutional violations.
Each option can be an initial step towards impeachment proceedings. None of the parties involved mentioned the prospect of impeachment.
"We are currently reviewing these options and also communicating with other political parties," said Muhammad Kholid, a senior official of the Prosperous Justice Party.
Most parties have reached a consensus that the two court rulings must be followed up by the parliament, he told Reuters.
Another party within Prabowo's camp, the National Awakening Party, is "seriously" considering the three options, said party official Muhammad Khozin in a statement.
Golkar Party lawmaker Ahmad Doli Kurnia said formally expressing their position would be the most relevant response to the courts' rulings, local media reported. Golkar, another party in Prabowo's coalition, has the second largest number of seats in parliament.
The vice president's office did not respond to a request for comment.
The only party outside Prabowo's coalition, Indonesian Democratic Party of Struggle, said recent public dissatisfaction stemming from Gibran's diploma, as well as the wiretapping cases, has prompted lawmakers to take action.
"There's increasingly intensive dialogue in the parliament to invoke their constitutional rights especially after the wiretapping," said the party's top official, Hasto Kristiyanto.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six dead, several injured in New York house fire
Article:
NEW YORK: Six people died in a house fire early Thursday in New York, authorities said, with Mayor Zohran Mamdani describing the blaze at a Brooklyn home as "devastating."
"I am heartbroken to announce that six New Yorkers lost their lives," Mamdani told reporters, noting that firefighters had responded in under four minutes.
Video from the scene showed orange flames roaring out of several windows at the row-style property in the Sunset Park neighbourhood, around eight kilometres from Manhattan.
"Four were dead upon FDNY's arrival, while two more passed away at the hospital.," Mamdani added, referring to the city's fire department. "All six were adults"
He said four civilians were also hurt, while three firefighters and two police officers suffered minor injuries.
Mamdani added that it was still too early to determine the cause of the fire, but the results of an investigation would be made public.
"This was a devastating fire. It will take a long time for this neighbourhood to mourn the neighbours they lost this morning, and to recover from this immense grief," he said.
Daniel Flynn, first deputy commissioner of the FDNY, said that fire marshalls were on the scene probing the blaze.
"This was a terrible tragedy, and hopefully we'll get a cause for you as soon as possible," he added.
Last month, four people died in the Bronx borough of New York after an electric bike battery caught fire inside an apartment. --AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Leaders should put younger generation ahead of personal interests
Article:
MELAKA: Political leaders must prioritise the future of the younger generation over personal wealth and interests, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the country's future depended on leaders committed to safeguarding public funds and ensuring children from all communities had access to better opportunities.
"I am a Malay and a Muslim. What do I stand to lose by showing that I care for Malay, Chinese and Indian children? They are all our children.
"If we look after everyone in this country, we can lift the nation. But if people keep stealing public funds to make two or three individuals rich, there will never be enough to go around," he said at a Pakatan Harapan campaign event in Paya Rumput.
Anwar said political leaders should look beyond their personal interests and consider the kind of country they would leave behind for future generations.
He said this was particularly important as Malaysia sought to strengthen its economy, attract foreign investment and equip young Malaysians with skills needed in emerging industries.
Citing Google's investment commitments in Malaysia, Anwar said he had stressed the importance of providing training opportunities for local talent, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI), information technology and computing.
"I want our children to be smarter than us. I want them to be skilled in AI, IT and computing. That is our responsibility.
"It is not about making noise or finding ways to make ourselves rich," he said.
Anwar said opportunities must be extended to Malaysians regardless of their racial or religious backgrounds.
He said protecting the interests of the Malay majority should not mean neglecting the needs of other communities.
He also expressed frustration over the increasingly hostile political discourse, saying politicians appeared more interested in trading insults than addressing issues affecting ordinary Malaysians.
"Sometimes we forget what really matters. We hear people insulting one another, calling others 'dajjal', 'celaka' and 'munafik'. What kind of politics is this?
"I am getting old. In another year, I will be 80. What I think about now is the future of our grandchildren, not just Anwar's grandchildren, but everyone's grandchildren.
"That is why I work hard. If people steal public funds, I will go after them. I do not care. I will continue fighting to protect this country," he said.

Title: #NSTviral: Strong winds send trader's stall rolling across road in Sepang

Title: Thailand fossil teeth reveal prehistoric 'giant rat' weighing 30kg
Article:
BANGKOK: A giant rodent weighing around 30 kilogrammes roamed what is now southern Thailand 33 to 35 million years ago, scientists said, after identifying a previously unknown species from two fossilised teeth.
The ancient animal, which one geologist on the team called a "giant rat", was among the largest known from the Paleogene period, offering new clues about how early rodents evolved to enormous sizes.
The findings, published Wednesday in the journal Scientific Reports, were based on a molar and an incisor discovered in 2004 at a coal mine in southern Krabi province.
Pannipa Tian, a geologist with Thailand's Department of Mineral Resources who found the incisor, said she initially misidentified the fossil because of its "unusually large size."
"At first, I thought it was a bone. I showed it to my supervisor, who told me it was a giant rat's tooth," Pannipa, 51, told AFP on Thursday.
The cream-coloured fossil stood out against the dark coal deposits, while another expedition member found the dark-coloured molar the same day.
The Krabi basin has previously yielded fossils of ancient primates, carnivores and hoofed mammals.
But at the time of the discovery, the team lacked sufficient evidence and technology to identify the species.
More than two decades later, researchers from Thailand, France and Canada were able to do so through detailed analysis of the teeth.
The animal weighed around 30 kilogrammes – an estimated half as much as a large capybara, the world's largest living rodent, they said.
Unlike the South American capybara, however, the prehistoric rodent belonged to the now-extinct Ischyromyidae family, one of the earliest major groups of rodents.
"It tells a lot about the diversity of life in the past," Pannipa said, suggesting that ancient rodents may have evolved in what is now Thailand before spreading to other parts of the world.
But with only two teeth recovered, the animal's appearance, diet and behaviour remain unknown.
The species was named Yakamys sirindhornae in honour of Thailand's Princess Sirindhorn, a supporter of scientific and palaeontological research.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka eyes exporting Kampung Digital model across Asean [WATCH]
Article:
MELAKA: The Melaka government intends to market its 'Kampung Digital' (Digital Village) model across the Asean region once the rural digitalisation initiative has been fully streamlined and upgraded.
Caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the model holds strong potential to be introduced to neighbouring countries as an innovative framework for residential address management and public service delivery.
He stressed, however, that the platform must undergo continuous refinement before it can be scaled up internationally.
"It must certainly be updated and enhanced to a standard where it can be marketed not only domestically, but also at the Asean level. We could potentially market it to Indonesia, Cambodia, Thailand, and Vietnam," he said.
He said this during a recording session of the Podcast Utama Edisi Khas Buletin TV3 for the 16th Melaka State Election.
Ab Rauf said 'Kampung Digital' was conceived to overcome structural flaws in traditional rural addressing, where hundreds of residents often shared a single generic postal address, complicating postal deliveries and emergency responses.
He said that the introduction of specific house numbers and QR codes allows residential properties to be pinpointed with pinpoint accuracy, assisting emergency rescue units and local authorities.
He noted that public sector technological adoption must accelerate so that government delivery mechanisms keep pace with commercial digital services.
"Digital development must stay aligned with the actual needs of the community.
"It is rather embarrassing that after nearly 70 years of nationhood, deliveries from Shopee, Lazada, McDonald's, and Grab can reach our doorsteps without fail, yet government letters cannot," he said.
Ab Rauf added that the digital addressing initiative has also been extended to cemetery management via the 'Kubur Digital' initiative, enabling heirs and family members to locate ancestral gravesites easily.
Furthermore, he said the state has introduced dedicated domain email accounts for every household registered under Kampung Digital, which will help streamline communications between schools and parents.
"Under my administration, the Melaka state government is offering a state domain by assigning an email address to every household under Kampung Digital.
"With these email addresses, the platform will interface with the Education Department, which I currently oversee, enabling teachers to connect directly with parents via email—for example, alerting them if a child has missed school for three consecutive days," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thailand bans textbook on national security grounds over monarchy content
Article:
BANGKOK: Thailand has banned a textbook about the country on national security grounds, with the tome's exiled editor saying Thursday it was outlawed over its content on the Thai monarchy.
The royal family holds revered status in Thai society and is shielded from criticism by a strict defamation law that critics say is used to muzzle dissent.
The book, a second edition of the "Routledge Handbook of Contemporary Thailand" published in English in August, was edited by Pavin Chachavalpongpun, a prominent academic and critic of the Thai monarchy who is based in Japan.
It contains chapters on Thailand's monarchy in the 21st century and the government's use of the lese-majeste law.
The book's first edition, released in 2019, was not banned, Pavin told AFP.
He said it was updated to "reflect changes in Thai politics" since 2020 youth-led pro-democracy protests, which featured unprecedented calls to reform the monarchy and the military.
The demonstrations were followed by a progressive party's election victory three years later that ended with its candidate being blocked from becoming prime minister by military-appointed senators and court challenges.
"Topics like this are why they decided to ban it," Pavin said in a telephone interview.
"Thailand's democracy is backsliding, and book bans are a clear indicator of that."
An order signed by National Police Chief Samran Nualma released on Wednesday said the book includes articles that "adversely affect national security and might cause unrest in the country."
Its content also "affects the security of the kingdom, public order or the good morals of the people", the order said.
Police have the authority to seize and destroy the book, it added.
Anyone found guilty of importing or distributing the book faces imprisonment of up to three years, a maximum fine of 60,000 baht (US$1,800), or both.
- BAN 'DOESN'T WORK' -
In a Facebook post, Pavin said the order helped promote the book.
"In the era of social media and the internet, a ban like this doesn't work," he wrote. "People might just skip the hard copy and get an ebook."
In 2023, his book, "Rama X: The Thai Monarchy under King Vajiralongkorn", was banned in a similar fashion.
Pavin is a former diplomat who has been out of Thailand since a 2014 military coup.
He said he was charged in 2020 for setting up a Facebook group that grew to more than two million members, who discuss the role of the royal family and the pro-democracy movement's proposals for reforms.
In August this year, campaign group Thai Lawyers for Human Rights said Pavin was among three people charged with lese-majeste over Facebook posts in the group the previous month.
Under Thailand's lese-majeste law, anyone convicted of insulting, defaming or threatening the king or his family can face a prison sentence of up to 15 years per offence.
Deputy government spokeswoman Lalida Persvivatana said in a statement to AFP that Thailand "prioritises maintaining national security and public order alongside respecting freedom of expression and academic freedom."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Resolving Melaka's flood woes remains one of my aspirations' —Ab Rauf [WATCH]
Article:
MELAKA: Tackling flood issues in Melaka remains a foremost priority for Caretaker Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, particularly in addressing deficiencies within the drainage network and mitigating the impact of rising water levels on residential settlements.
He said the state administration has initiated several measures alongside relevant agencies to enhance water drainage systems, including securing Federal Government funding for flood mitigation schemes.
He noted that several flood-prone areas have been identified as requiring urgent intervention, including Bukit Rambai, which received dedicated allocations under the national budget.
"With regard to flooding, we have sought substantial allocations from the Federal Government. We have upgraded flood mitigation measures to improve the discharge of runoff from flood-hit localities.
"In Masjid Tanah, for instance, we will receive an allocation exceeding RM430 million to implement a systematic flood mitigation scheme," he said during a recording session of the Podcast Utama Edisi Khas Buletin TV3 for the 16th Melaka State Election.
"Other areas, such as the flood-prone Bukit Rambai, were also granted special funds under the Prime Minister's recent budget presentation," he added.
Ab Rauf pointed out that flood risks in Melaka are partly attributable to legacy development planning that failed to fully consider the impact of rising water levels on housing estates.
"The whole of Melaka is susceptible to flooding because past town planning did not anticipate that rising water levels would affect residential areas," he said.
High tide phenomena, he said, often cause sea levels to exceed river levels, preventing runoff from discharging effectively into the sea.
"Runoff flows from residential areas into rivers, and from rivers into the sea. When high tides occur, the sea level rises above the river level, causing backflow. That is what triggers the floods.
"We are actively studying methods to resolve this. It remains my top priority to resolve Melaka's flood problems," he said.
On his commitment should he be returned to office, Ab Rauf affirmed that putting an end to the state's flooding woes remains a deeply personal ambition.
"One of my lifelong dreams is to put an end to the flood problems in Melaka," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: Bersatu candidate demands public apology over old viral video
Article:
MELAKA: A Bersatu candidate in the state election has given those responsible for circulating a video linking him to an altercation with a local authority officer 24 hours to issue a public apology and clear his name, failing which he will take legal action.
Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee, who is contesting the Pengkalan Batu seat, said the video, which went viral on Threads, was an old recording, although he could not recall the exact date of the incident.
"The video is very old. I am giving them 24 hours from the time it started circulating. If my name is not cleared, legal action will be taken.
"I do not need to make a fuss. There is the law. That is all," he said when contacted.
Norhizam was commenting on the video, which allegedly showed him arguing with a local authority officer attempting to seize potted plants at the back of his house on the grounds that they were obstructing access.
He said the recirculation of the video had tarnished his reputation as he was contesting the Pengkalan Batu seat again in the Melaka election.
He also alleged that the move was a form of "psychological warfare" by parties concerned about his return to the political contest in the constituency.

Title: BN-PN understanding at a good level, says Ab Rauf [WATCH]
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) will unveil a joint manifesto for the first time today in conjunction with the 16th Melaka State Election, aiming to secure more than 21 of the 28 State Legislative Assembly seats.
Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the manifesto would serve as a comprehensive pledge offering substantial benefits to the people of the state.
"This manifesto will certainly deliver returns to the people. Much like our 2021 manifesto, we have fulfilled nearly 90 per cent of what was pledged.
"As this is the first manifesto combined with PN, I cannot provide any teasers just yet, as it is still in the final stages of refinement before being presented to the public this Friday (tomorrow)," he said.
He said this during a recording session of the Podcast Utama Edisi Khas Buletin TV3 for the 16th Melaka State Election.
Commenting on the cooperation between the two coalitions, Ab Rauf said the mutual understanding between BN and PN not only encompasses the coordination of campaign machinery, but also extends to policy formulation.
"We see that the understanding between BN and PN is very strong. This rapport has been translated into cohesive campaign machinery, unified voter engagement, and well-aligned policy-making.
"If you ask me, this is a solid consensus aimed at safeguarding the welfare of the people," he said.
Ab Rauf added that BN has set a baseline target of 21 seats for the state election, with aspirations to increase that tally through cooperation with strategic partners.
"The baseline is 21 seats, and we will endeavour to improve upon that to secure more than 21 seats through our strategic partners who have been fielded to contest," he said.
However, when asked about potential post-election portfolio allocations should the coalition secure the mandate, he declined to make any premature announcements.
"I cannot disclose that at this juncture because we must win first," he said.
Ab Rauf stressed that the immediate priority is ensuring that the pact between both coalitions translates into achieving the seat targets set for the polls.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke: Defeating BN-PN in Melaka polls no easy feat
Article:
MELAKA: Overcoming Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional will be no easy feat, particularly as political rivals seek to consolidate their strength amid multi-cornered contests.
DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said he hoped voters in Melaka would consolidate their ballots behind PH to avoid split votes that could inadvertently hand victory to their rivals.
He said the emergence of new, splinter parties contesting in three-to-four-cornered fights serves only to fragment the opposition vote, effectively paving the way for a BN and PN victory.
"Defeating BN and Perikatan Nasional is not easy. While new parties have every right to contest, voting for them will only dilute our strength.
"They cannot win, but they can hand victory straight to Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional," he said.
Loke was addressing supporters during the Malam Harapan 2026 event, here, that drew a turnout of more than 1,000 people.
Political arrogance, he said, must not take root ahead of the polls, especially when there are claims that PH strongholds such as Bukit Katil and Ayer Keroh could be taken from them.
To safeguard democratic governance in the state assembly, he said DAP has set its sights on defending its four seats (Kota Laksamana, Bandar Hilir, Kesidang, and Ayer Keroh) while mounting an aggressive challenge in Pengkalan Batu, Duyong and Gadek.
Loke said voters should not let one bloc have unbridled dominance without an effective check-and-balance mechanism as it risk returning the state to an era of unchecked power and complacency.
